summary: Tested Lex model switch + Lex learning loop end-to-end (backend pytest 14 tests + Playwright UI on mobile/desktop). Free tier Lex chat returns model claude-haiku-5-5 (/api/lex/chat and /api/lex/chat/stream meta event); DB conversations.model_used=claude-haiku-5-5, no 'Primary model failed' fallbacks in logs. Feedback endpoint: 401/403 without auth, 400 invalid rating, 'wrong' drafts a pending lesson (source=report) in ~5s. Admin lex-lessons: list/stats, add (400 if <10 chars), approve, edit, remove, invalid status 400, 404 unknown id, non-admin 403. Approved lesson PINEAPPLE-42 injected into prompt -> Lex replied 'The test code word is PINEAPPLE-42' (then deleted). Cron /api/cron/lex-learning 401 without/with bad bearer, 200 queued with secret. UI: thumbs/flag buttons under every Lex reply, thumbs-up toast + all three disabled, Report wrong opens aa-prompt and shows 'Reported' + toast; Admin 'Lex's Brain' card approve/edit/add/remove/run-now all work. Regression: sanity-soon-{i} shows 'Solicitor check · Coming soon'; Lex says 'It is 2026. Today is Tuesday 3 November 2026', next tax year 6 April 2027 (correct).

minor.issue: /app/.emergent/cron/webhook-crons only schedules deadline-reminders and review-requests. There is NO weekly lex-learning cron registered, so the weekly job never runs automatically (only 'Check for new lessons now' does).

Dedup is exact-text only and there is no lock on weekly_job. Running cron + run-now together (or two runs) produces near-duplicate pending lessons (e.g. two almost identical 'Crime and Policing Act 2026 ... 6 November 2026' law_watch lessons are now in the pending queue).
No rate limit: every 'wrong' rating spawns a Sonnet 5.5 LLM call, so cost can be abused. Question/answer text comes from the client and is trusted, not looked up from the stored conversation.
When the primary model fails and the Sonnet 4.5 fallback answers, response 'model', model_used and cost tracking still record the primary model_id. Observability is wrong.

Approved lessons live in an in-process _cache. With more than one uvicorn worker or pod in production, approve/remove only refreshes the worker that handled the request, so other workers keep serving stale lessons until they restart.
Returns 200 for ids that do not exist (no 404).

ui_bugs.issue: In the first Playwright run on mobile, clicking lex-thumb-up-1 straight after the reply rendered (without scrolling it into view) did nothing: no feedback request, no toast. After scroll_into_view it worked every time. Possibly flaky or a re-render race. Low priority.

issues: Reject/Remove act instantly with no confirm or undo. Removing a live lesson is a one-click destructive action.
With many pending lessons the card gets very long inside the Settings modal. Consider collapsing it or capping its height.

action_items: Register the weekly lex-learning webhook cron (e.g. Monday 07:00 -> POST /api/cron/lex-learning). It is currently missing from webhook-crons.
Add a lock or 'already running' guard to weekly_job, and use fuzzier dedup (normalised text or similarity) to avoid near-duplicate pending lessons.
Rate-limit /api/lex/feedback 'wrong' reports per user per day.
Report the actual model used when the fallback fires.
Optional: refresh the lessons cache from the DB on a TTL so multi-worker prod stays consistent. Add a confirm before Remove.
critical_code_review_comments: lex_lessons.py is clean and small. Approval gating works: pending lessons are not injected and only status=approved goes into _cache.
Fallback path model reporting is incorrect (see minor).
In-memory cache is not safe across multiple workers.

success_rate.backend: 100% (14/14; the stream test first failed on my wrong assertion, fixed: model is in the 'meta' event)

My cron + run-now triggers also drafted a few law_watch pending lessons that can't be told apart from existing ones, so they were left (pending now: 9 law_watch + 1 report). test@advocate.app hit its 5/5 free daily Lex limit today because of these tests.
